data.title: AI shopping gains ground as Salesforce sees Black Friday sales hitting $83B
data.description:
Black Friday is on track to remain the biggest shopping day of the year, with global online sales expected to reach $83 billion, while artificial intelligence is playing an increasingly prominent role in how consumers find and buy products.

Salesforce (CRM) expects worldwide online spending to rise 5% year over year, with U.S. sales reaching $18.7 billion, up 4%. The forecast follows a record Thanksgiving, when online purchases totaled $37.2 billion globally, up 4.6%, including $8.8 billion in the U.S.

AI is becoming a bigger part of that shopping activity. Nearly one-quarter of holiday orders so far have been influenced by AI, while referral traffic from AI agent channels jumped 75% from a year earlier. One in five shoppers now starts their shopping journey with an AI tool.

Retailers could also be seeing bigger orders from shoppers using their AI assistants. Consumers who interacted with a brand-owned shopping agent on Thanksgiving spent 43% more per order than those who did not.

The AI landscape is shifting, too. Gemini (GOOG) has overtaken ChatGPT (OPENAI) in global traffic share, although ChatGPT remains the leading AI channel in the U.S.

Social shopping also gained ground, with TikTok Shop (TIKTOK) orders surging 332% year over year on Thanksgiving. Social media accounted for 23% of global ecommerce traffic, up 18%, while the share of orders originating from social referrals climbed 34% to 6.3%.

Appliances were the fastest-growing global shopping category, with online sales rising 27%, followed by active footwear and active apparel. In the U.S., active apparel and footwear led category growth at 21%, while home sales increased 19%.

Meanwhile, bots and crawlers accounted for 30% of Thanksgiving ecommerce traffic. Mobile devices generated 82% of global online traffic and 73% of orders.

data.title: Dallas Fed's 12-month Trimmed Mean PCE inflation rate rises in October
data.description:
Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas' 12-month Trimmed Mean PCE inflation rate rose to 2.4% in October from 2.3% in September.

The Trimmed Mean PCE inflation rate is an alternative measure of core inflation in the price index for personal consumption expenditures. 

Core PCE inflation rate, which excludes food and energy, was 3.3% over the 12-month period ending in October 26, compared to 3.1% as of September 26.

Headline PCE inflation rate was 3.8% in October, compared to 3.7% in the previous month.

data.title: Amazon has wall-to-wall free sports coverage on Black Friday
data.description:
Amazon (AMZN) is going bigger with its Black Friday sports marathon, which is now a regular part of its live-event strategy. The lineup includes golf, the NFL, and the NBA. Notably, viewers don't need a subscription or Prime membership to watch any of the sports coverage barrage. The company's goal is to add new Prime Video or Amazon Prime subscribers.

The day starts with the return of The Skins Game, kicking off roughly 15 hours of live programming. The field is Wyndham Clark, Brooks Koepka, and Justin Thomas, who have 31 PGA Tour wins between them, plus rookie Jackson Koivun. Next is Amazon's (AMZN) fourth Black Friday NFL game, Broncos vs. Steelers. The night ends with an NBA doubleheader featuring the defending champion Knicks and the Western Conference champion Spurs. 

The football game also comes with some drama after Pittsburgh benched Aaron Rodgers on Tuesday. On Wednesday he criticized coach Mike McCarthy on The Pat McAfee Show, and the Steelers released him. Front Office Sports expects the fallout to bring more eyes to a game between two playoff contenders.

Amazon (AMZN) is facing a tough comparison from a year ago when the Chicago Bears-Philadelphia Eagles game averaged 16.3M viewers, up 21% from 2024 and 70% from the 2023 debut. The 2025 NBA doubleheader averaged 2.09M, up 121%. Last year's marathon was Amazon's (AMZN) biggest single day of live sports ever, so this year's slate has a high bar to clear.

data.title: Market 'delicately poised' after narrow AI unwind - Goldman
data.description:
A crowded, narrow momentum trade centered on AI (AIQ) (AIEQ) has unraveled into a sharp market drawdown as technical selling and shifting sentiment leave equities (SPY) (QQQ) (DIA) "delicately poised," according to Bobby Molavi of Goldman Sachs.

The past four to six weeks have delivered a material drawdown led by an AI trade unwind and positioning degross, with investor sentiment swinging from hope to fear and, at points, panic, Molavi wrote in a note published Friday. Despite stellar earnings—Nvidia's (NVDA) recent results among them—investors have reset their willingness to pay elevated multiples on the sustainability of future capex, earnings, and cash flows.

For much of the year, the market buffered AI-related declines through sector rotation: hyperscalers (META) (AMZN) (GOOG) (GOOGL) (MSFT) dropping, offset by gains in staples, travel and leisure, and real estate. But that rotation effect cracked as short covering slowed and then stopped, the VIX (VIX) spiked from its 15–20 anchor into a new 25–30 corridor, and market breadth collapsed with broader tech exposure reaching 60%–70%.

The mechanical selling that followed was swift and unforgiving. CTAs, risk parity, and vol control strategies—once passive holders—turned aggressive sellers when volatility rallied and technical levels breached, creating a supply wave too heavy for the market to absorb.

Molavi laid out the pillars to watch going forward: rates, where the Federal Reserve appears behind the curve; credit, where the spread between B and CCC high-yield bonds has hit 8%—a threshold breached fewer than five times since 1996 and historically associated with S&P 500 drawdowns exceeding 11.5%; volatility, which needs to reset lower before confidence can return; and AI itself, which requires tangible return on investment and productivity metrics before share price momentum can resume.

Since the COVID lows of March 2020, the S&P 500 has rallied 250% through a litany of crises—but near-term credit and volatility stability remain essential. As Molavi put it: "Equity can hurt you...debt can kill you."

data.title: Black Friday came early for retailers as Thanksgiving delivered record $7.1B in sales
data.description:
Shoppers chasing double-digit discounts on electronics, toys, sporting goods, and apparel turned Thanksgiving into a record day for retailers—and put Black Friday on pace for one too.

Adobe Analytics found that shoppers worked off their Thanksgiving gluttony online, spending a record $7.1B online—up 10.4% from last year. That still trails the forecasts for Black Friday ($12.9B) and Cyber Monday ($15.1B), but Thanksgiving’s growth rate beat both.

Adobe credits this to deep discounts that were pulled forward from Black Friday and Cyber Monday. The biggest discounts were on electronics and toys, with attractive offers for everything else, including furniture and appliances, and expected to become even more appealing during Black Friday.

No doubt Grand Theft Auto VI (TTWO) drove a surge in gaming sales, with the sale of consoles soaring more than 1,000% (GTA VI is only compatible with certain consoles). Triple-digit percentage gains were also seen in video games and accessories.

And while Cyber Monday is typically the day shoppers’ cash in on deals for electronics, sales on Thanksgiving were equally impressive with buyers scooping up smartphones, headphones, smartwatches, TVs, and other smart appliances, driving sales up by 250% to more than 600% from last year.

The proliferation of AI shopping bots generated more purchases and created larger carts and reportedly drove a 92% increase in revenue per visit compared to non-AI traffic. The use of AI also means fewer returns for retailers to handle after the holidays. Adobe found that one-third of respondents were less likely to return an item that they found using AI.

Shoppers also took advantage of the Buy-Now-Pay-Later (BNPL) option, increasing by 5.1% from last year and expected to drive a record $1.09B in online spending on Cyber Monday.

Extrapolating Thanksgiving spending to the next major shopping days of the holiday season, Adobe expects Black Friday spending to reach another record of $12.9B—or $13.7M per minute between 10am and 2pm—and Cyber Monday to a record $15.1B, adding to the $47.5B expected to be spent during Cyber Week (5-day period including Thanksgiving). 

Some of the top sellers are Pokémon Pikachu Puppertronic, squishies, LEGO Pokémon Smart Play, Grand Theft Auto VI (TTWO), Madden NFL 27 (EA), Nintendo Switch 2 (NTDOY) (NTDOF), PlayStation 5 (SONY), Xbox Series S/X (MSFT), iPhone Duo (AAPL), Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 (SSNLF), Oura Ring (OURA), AirPods (AAPL), and Ray-Ban Meta (META) smartglasses. 

The takeaway: Thanksgiving was just the warm-up. Between pulled-forward deals, GTA VI mania, and AI doing the shopping, retailers are headed for their biggest Cyber Week ever.

data.title: Anthropic shares extend gains, recovering from post-IPO slump
data.description:
Anthropic (ANT) shares surged roughly 9% at $90.06 on Friday, recovering from a rocky start to life as a publicly traded company.

The stock had snapped a three-session losing streak on Wednesday, ending 1.08% higher ahead of the Thanksgiving break but remained below IPO price. 

Three consecutive sessions of losses had pushed shares to $81.9, below their $83 IPO price, wiping out the gains from its much-anticipated Nasdaq debut.

In its Nasdaq debut on Nov. 19, the stock opened at $111.50 and hit an intraday high of $115.10.

Anthropic has struggled to join the broader AI rally that briefly lifted technology stocks following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's dramatic return to the company. While the rally boosted sentiment across the AI trade, Anthropic shares largely missed out.

Investors have raised concerns about Anthropic's $900B spending commitments, while bond investors expect its debt to receive a junk rating.

"We believe Anthropic's financial success will be driven by three key factors. First is whether the firm is able to scale enterprise adoption of its models. Second is whether its models continue to improve and unlock economically useful capabilities.Third, even if the artificial intelligence ecosystem creates a ton of value, is whether Anthropic is able to capture some of this value using a mixture of models, products, and services. We remain confident that the firm will be able to execute on all three fronts," said Malik Ahmed Khan of Morningstar as he maintains a "fair price" of $92 on ANT stock.

Anthropic's IPO had strengthened its ability to meet rising computing costs, as per Morningstar. The company raised more than $100B through the listing and has $132B in cash on its balance sheet, which Morningstar believes could help it meet its computing commitments in 2027 and 2028 even if revenue growth slows.

data.title: China’s big tech value falls to record-low share of U.S. peers
data.description:
China’s biggest technology companies have continued to lose ground to their U.S. counterparts during the market selloff, with their combined market value falling to a record-low 11.6% of that of Alphabet (GOOG) (GOOGL), Amazon (AMZN), and Meta Platforms (META), according to market strategist Rob Anderson.

The combined market capitalization of Baidu (BIDU), Alibaba (BABA), and Tencent (TCEHY) stood at $829.78B as of Nov. 25, compared with $7.14T for the three U.S. technology companies, data from Ned Davis Research showed.

That put the Chinese group’s value at 11.63% of its U.S. peers, the lowest since at least September 2014, when the Ned Davis Research data begin.

The latest reading is well below the 40.61% average for the ratio over the full period, according to the chart. The ratio came close to 80% in 2015 and again in 2020-21 before its subsequent decline.

data.title: Regeneron gains approval of Lynozyfic in UK
data.description:
• The UK's Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency has approved Regeneron Pharmaceuticals' (REGN) Lynozyfic (linvoseltamab) for multiple myeloma.
  • It was approved for patients with the bone marrow cancer who have failed on at least three prior therapies, including  an immunomodulatory agent, a proteasome inhibitor, and an anti-CD38 antibody.
  • Approval was based on data from a trial that found ~71% of patients had a response to treatment, from partial responses to complete responses. About 50% had a complete response with an average duration of 29 months.

data.title: Ten top-rated consumer discretionary stocks as BofA signals a sector rotation
data.description:
According to BofA Research, a shift toward consumer discretionary stocks and away from consumer staples could offer a contrarian investment opportunity as slowing capital expenditure potentially benefits margins in services and homebuilding while keeping interest rates and mortgage costs contained.

BofA Research also sees a potential pick-up in residential real estate transactions in 2027 as a possible catalyst for big-ticket spending, following a prolonged period without a meaningful housing cycle since the COVID-19 pandemic.

The shift in sector positioning comes as the U.S. enters the holiday shopping season, with Black Friday taking place today.

According to the National Retail Federation, an estimated 182.7 million Americans plan to shop between Thanksgiving Day and Cyber Monday, while around 69% of consumers, or approximately 126 million people, intend to shop on Black Friday. Despite persistent inflation and affordability concerns, the NRF expects holiday sales during November and December to exceed $1 trillion for the first time, representing 4.2% growth over 2025.

However, budget-conscious consumers are increasingly looking for deals and opting for less expensive gifts, potentially creating a mixed demand environment for discretionary retailers.

Against this backdrop, the following list highlights the top 10 consumer discretionary stocks ranked by Seeking Alpha's Quant Ratings. The screen spans several industries within the sector, including apparel retail, specialty retail, footwear and broadline retail.

Abercrombie & Fitch Co. (ANF) leads the list with a near-perfect Quant Rating of 4.99. Victoria's Secret & Co. (VSXY) and GigaCloud Technology Inc. (GCT) follow with ratings of 4.92 and 4.91, respectively. Academy Sports and Outdoors, Inc. (ASO) and Frontdoor, Inc. (FTDR) round out the top five. Amazon.com, Inc. (AMZN), the largest company on the list with a market capitalization of $2.64 trillion, ranks tenth with a Quant Rating of 4.81. All 10 stocks carry a Strong Buy rating under Seeking Alpha's quantitative system.

Seeking Alpha's Quant Ratings system grades stocks on their relative performance on key quantitative metrics. It hones in on stocks with the strongest combination of value, growth, profitability, EPS revisions and price momentum relative to their sector peers.
